Round 1 review of spec pose-read-view-streamed-object-digests (an engine consistency fix: the governance read view's retained captured-input budget was being exceeded by `pose index` because every change set read `git show --binary` of every attributed commit only to hash it).

What to judge: a Git object read whose bytes a producer only hashes is streamed into the producer and the read view retains only its digest and length, under a separate streamed budget (8 GiB per operation, again for the audit, 256 MiB per read); a second read in the same operation streams again and leaves the producer unknown if it differs; the final audit skips a commit patch read by full id only while the root's effective Git configuration is the one it was read under; change-set diff digests and ids are unchanged (the same bytes enter the same hash; on the real pose-dist corpus the whole delivery-integrity.json was byte-identical before and after); the captured-input budget returns to 512 MiB by amendment D11 of ADR governance-reads-use-bounded-operation-scoped-views, superseding D10. Measurements are in the spec's execution log; reproducing them needs the full pose-dist history and minutes of I/O.

Do NOT run `pose assess`, `pose state`, `pose index` or anything else that writes under `.pose/`; dispose assess-* tools from the sealed evidence and the code. Leave the worktree as you found it.
